A whole-genome pangenome is too large to load into R.
[gfa-to-tabix](https://github.com/GMOD/gfa-to-tabix) indexes it once by
reference coordinate, and ggbandage reads the graph of one region from that
index.

- **In:** a pangenome GFA, indexed once by gfa-to-tabix, as a local file or a
  url
- **Out:** the graph of one region, as a figure, as GFA for other tools, or as
  a syng graph of that region
- ggbandage downloads the blocks under the region and no more. A cut at
  KIV-2 with five haplotypes takes about 3 s from the hosted 1.2 GB HPRC walk
  file

## Two kinds of index

|            | Walk file                                   | Segment index                                       |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Input GFA  | base-level, with W or P lines               | an rGFA (`*.sv.gfa.gz`), or a plain GFA with `--reference` |
| Command    | `gfa-to-tabix graph.gfa --walks --refs GRCh38 -o graph` | `gfa-to-tabix graph.sv.gfa.gz -o graph` |
| Files      | `graph.GRCh38.walks.bed.gz` and its `.tbi`  | `graph.graph.bed.gz` and its `.tbi`                 |
| Holds      | every haplotype's walk through the region   | the segments and links under the region             |
| Draw it as | walks lifted or faceted, and walk rows      | the graph's shape, over megabases                   |

`bandage_layout()` and `bandage_gfa()` read either file, given a `region`.
`bandage_walk_rows()` needs a walk file.

gfa-to-tabix before 2.0, or with `--format 1`, writes a segment index as two
files, `graph.segs.bed.gz` and `graph.links.bed.gz`. ggbandage reads that
pair too, given the `.segs.bed.gz` or the prefix `graph`.

## Making a walk file

1. Convert the graph to GFA if it ships as `.gbz`, as HPRC's do:

   ```console
   vg convert -f graph.gbz > graph.gfa
   ```

2. Index it, naming the genome whose coordinates `region` will use:

   ```console
   gfa-to-tabix graph.gfa --walks --refs GRCh38 -o graph
   ```

3. Read it from disk, or put the `.walks.bed.gz` and `.tbi` on a web server.
   A server that answers range requests, as Amazon S3 does, sends each block
   ggbandage asks for. One without range support, such as
   `python -m http.server`, sends the whole file on every read

## Reading a region

```{r read, eval = FALSE}
library(ggbandage)

walks <- "https://jbrowse.org/demos/hprc/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38-f5s.GRCh38.walks.bed.gz"
g <- bandage_layout(walks, region = "chr1:196,640,001-196,900,000", haplotypes = c("HG00097#1", "HG02055#1"))
```

- `region` takes a locus as a genome browser writes it. `"chr6"` stands for
  `GRCh38#0#chr6` when exactly one sequence ends that way
- `haplotypes` picks the `sample#haplotype` walks to cut, every one by default
- `context` keeps that many bp of reference past each end, 1,000 by default

## Exporting a region

`bandage_gfa()` returns the region as GFA text, so the cut can feed any tool
that reads GFA, such as odgi or ggtubemap's `read_gfa()`:

```{r export, eval = FALSE}
gfa <- bandage_gfa(walks, region = "chr6:160,616,004-160,646,753", haplotypes = c("HG00097#1", "HG00133#2"))
writeLines(gfa, "kiv2.gfa")
```

Each W line names the haplotype's contig and its span there, such as
`W HG00133 2 CM090065.1 162127148 162293018`, so the cut also locates each
haplotype's sequence in its assembly.

## A syng graph of a region

`scripts/build-syng-region.sh` in the source repository builds a
[syng](https://github.com/richarddurbin/syng) graph of one region from the
HPRC walk file, with no alignment step:

```console
scripts/build-syng-region.sh chr1:25,250,000-25,450,000 rhd HG01258#2,HG01106#1
```

1. `bandage_gfa()` cuts the region, and its W lines give each haplotype's
   contig span
2. The script fetches each span from GenBank, and GRCh38's and CHM13's from
   UCSC, all on GRCh38's strand
3. [impg](https://github.com/pangenome/impg) builds the syng graph and writes
   `rhd.syng.gfa.gz`

ggbandage ships the RHD graph the script built, and the gallery draws it:

```{r syng, eval = FALSE}
rhd <- system.file("extdata", "rhd.syng.gfa.gz", package = "ggbandage")
autoplot(bandage_layout(rhd))
```

- `IMPG` names the impg binary, `impg` on the `PATH` by default
- The [developing notes](https://github.com/GMOD/ggbandage/blob/main/docs/developing.md)
  cover how the cut reaches V8, and timings on the HPRC segment index
